analysis:
Examined units: docs/architecture/inference.md head 2395-2647 (Flint, Bonsai and GLM tool-output text) and docs/developer/test.md (base text plus the patch). Unit 9bceb6d953b336e2:15 lies outside the head changed ranges (3, 684-691, 818-821, 837, 884-903, 1740-1759), so it is unchanged context. It restates Flint fail-closed tool/JSON validation and logprob filtering of withheld reasoning; I found no regression there.

The test.md changes are documentation only. They describe four new test areas:
(1) GLM5Next logprobs capture on the protected native bridge; MiMo keeps its typed 400.
(2) A verified-weight-hash path. GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256 publishes the manifest aggregate only after every file verifies. This replaces separate load-time WeightHasher passes.
(3) VerifiedWeightHashStore, whose record path the runner sets via DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE (test.md head ~129-143).
(4) OpenRouter capability tests that check content-free 422s.

Security-relevant behavior described in inference.md head 684-691, which is in another batch: on the next coordinator-mode start the provider registers the stored hash without reading the weights. It relies on file device, inode, size, mtime and ctime staying unchanged, and the load re-verifies before serving.

This relates to A-004, T-012 and T-027 (operator weight substitution, ADV-001). The registration-time weight hash now rests on a stat-metadata cache that the operator can influence: the store file location, and potentially an env override in production. The ctime/inode assumption also does not hold against a root operator writing raw blocks or manipulating the clock. The doc says the load re-verifies before serving, so the serving-time hash should still be bound to the bytes. However, the source for VerifiedWeightHashStore, ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash and the registration path is not supplied.

Integration should verify:
(a) whether DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE is honored in production builds, and whether the store file is owner-only and authenticated (e.g. a MAC under an SE-rooted key) rather than plain JSON;
(b) whether a mismatch at load-time re-verification withdraws or refreshes the advertised hash before routing;
(c) whether the threat model's A-004 and T-012 text needs an update for the cached registration hash.

GLM logprobs relay remains inside the encrypted response path (A-001); no new exposure is evident. I made no finding because the implementation evidence is absent.
